section_summary: This section follows U.S. monitoring of Japanese crab canneries in the Bering Sea and concern that their vessels might begin fishing for Alaskan salmon. It includes Coast Guard observations, diplomatic inquiries, discussions with Japanese fishing executives, and reports alleging intelligence gathering in the Aleutian Islands. Later records concern Japanese boats seized in Philippine waters, brief cross-references to other fisheries matters, and the opening of a report on a Soviet-Japanese dispute over fishery rentals.

subfiles.title: Status inquiry before Ambassador Grew's arrival
subfiles.from: James Grafton Rogers, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks Commerce's agreement with a memorandum on Japanese fishing near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Requests confirmation before briefing Grew.

subfiles.title: Commerce confirms fisheries memorandum
subfiles.about: Confirms that the State Department's memorandum reflects Commerce's understanding.
subfiles.summary: Promises to notify Commissioner O'Malley and report developments.

subfiles.title: Report of fishing gear near Amak Island
subfiles.about: Reports an apparently Japanese steamer and tenders fishing near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: Commerce asks for Japanese vessel information through the embassy and emphasizes concern about possible salmon fishing.

subfiles.title: Reply on Amak Island sighting
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Amak Island report and refers it to the embassy.
subfiles.summary: Promises to forward information received from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Instruction to inquire into Japanese fishing
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests a full report on Japanese fishing vessels off Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Encloses earlier correspondence and asks about vessel movements and activities.

subfiles.title: Reply on Nagato Maru sighting
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a Coast Guard report that Nagato Maru had nine boats near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: Says the report was sent to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Nagato Maru boat-count inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards a report that Nagato Maru carried nine boats, differing from an earlier account.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the difference between nine boats observed and two auxiliary boats reported.

subfiles.title: Departure of Nagato Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Nagato Maru's departure for crab fishing in Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Names Kasuga Maru and Ise Maru as its two auxiliary motor boats.

subfiles.title: Identification of the vessel near Amak Island
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Identifies Nagato Maru as the probable vessel seen near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Neville's despatch on its crab-fishing voyage.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard report on Nagato Maru
subfiles.from: E. F. Morgan, Acting Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Relays a Coast Guard sighting of Nagato Maru and nine boats near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the patrol boat Montgomery was observing the vessel.

subfiles.title: Japanese assurance about Nagato Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese statements that Nagato Maru alone was authorized to fish off Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities say the vessel is equipped only for crab fishing and canning, and that salmon or halibut fishing would be unprofitable.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Montgomery cruise report
subfiles.about: Forwards the Coast Guard's detailed observations of Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter for the Montgomery cruise report.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard endorsement of cruise report
subfiles.about: Forwards Montgomery's June 17–24 cruise report.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the report for information.

subfiles.title: Bering Sea Patrol endorsement
subfiles.about: Forwards Montgomery's cruise report and requests a copy for Fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Requests distribution to the Commissioner of Fisheries.

subfiles.title: Montgomery cruise report, June 17–24
subfiles.about: Describes Nagato Maru's crab-fishing operation near Amak Island.
subfiles.summary: The patrol observed the cannery, its tenders and small boats, a supply ship, and extensive crab nets. The report estimates catches, staffing, fishing grounds, and seasonal movements, and says the operation remained beyond the three-mile limit.

subfiles.title: State reply on Montgomery report
subfiles.from: James Grafton Rogers, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Montgomery report and shares Grew's information on Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the cruise findings were sent to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Montgomery report sent to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce's letter and the Coast Guard report on Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: Sends the documents for the ambassador's information.

subfiles.title: Japanese patrol boat to inspect Nagato Maru
subfiles.about: Reports that Shunkotsu Maru will sail to Bristol Bay to survey Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese patrol boat is expected to leave the Kamchatka coast around July 29.

subfiles.title: Japanese patrol plan relayed to Commerce
subfiles.from: James Grafton Rogers, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew's telegram concerning Shunkotsu Maru's planned inspection.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the July 27 telegram.

subfiles.title: Explanation of Nagato Maru's small boats
subfiles.about: Explains why earlier Japanese information omitted eight small fishing boats.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says eight Kawasaki-sen were ordinary equipment for a floating cannery, distinct from its two auxiliary motor launches.

subfiles.title: Small-boat explanation sent to Commerce
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew's explanation of boats accompanying Nagato Maru.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the August 2 despatch.

subfiles.title: Chart of Nagato Maru's location
subfiles.about: Forwards a tracing showing Nagato Maru and auxiliary boats on August 6.
subfiles.summary: The chart came from the Alaska Packers Association.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of vessel chart
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the chart of Nagato Maru's location.
subfiles.summary: Says the chart was sent to the ambassador in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Vessel chart sent to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards the chart tracing of Nagato Maru and its boats.
subfiles.summary: The observation was made on August 6, 1932.

subfiles.title: Invitation to crab-industry meeting
subfiles.about: Invites a State Department representative to meet Japanese crab-industry executives.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the meeting correspondence.

subfiles.title: O'Malley agrees to receive Japanese visitors
subfiles.about: Agrees to meet Ueki and Takasaki on October 17.
subfiles.summary: Offers to assist their discussions of crab-industry cooperation.

subfiles.title: Introduction of Japanese crab executives
subfiles.about: Introduces Ueki and Takasaki and requests a meeting.
subfiles.summary: They seek advice on closer Japanese-American cooperation in the crab-meat industry.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment note
subfiles.about: Records Miss Hanna's view that a letter needs no acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: A brief internal handling note.

subfiles.title: Press-release routing note
subfiles.about: Notes an expected War Department press release based on the governor general's report.
subfiles.summary: An internal note on handling the Philippine fishing-boat incident.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Philippine fishing-boat arrests
subfiles.about: Summarizes the arrest of Japanese fishermen in Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: Recommends no State Department action on a routine Philippine law violation.

subfiles.title: War Department transmits governor general's radiogram
subfiles.about: Forwards a radiogram about two Japanese fishing boats seized in Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter for the incident account.

subfiles.title: Radiogram on Arayat's seizure of fishing boats
subfiles.from: Governor General of the Philippine Islands
subfiles.about: Reports the pursuit and detention of two Japanese boats near Fuga Island.
subfiles.summary: The Arayat detained 34 crew members; rough weather prevented towing their boats. The governor general planned to treat the incident as a routine customs violation.

subfiles.title: Note on proposed fisheries meeting
subfiles.about: Seeks instructions on attending O'Malley's meeting about Japanese Bering Sea fishing.
subfiles.summary: Reports O'Malley's invitation for October 17.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Japanese crab executives
subfiles.about: Records a meeting about Japanese-American cooperation in Alaskan crab fishing.
subfiles.summary: Japanese executives describe licenses, declining crab catches, costs, and possible cooperation with American businesses. Takasaki warns that unprofitable crab fishing could lead Japanese vessels to pursue salmon. Bureau officials suspect the proposed arrangement aims to reduce tariff costs.

subfiles.title: Conversation on American vessel requirements
subfiles.about: Records Ueki's questions about using an American vessel to land crab meat.
subfiles.summary: Tyrer discusses vessel origin, officers, crew language, immigration, and duty-free entry. Ueki decides to consult a lawyer.

subfiles.title: Bureau of Fisheries discussion after Japanese visit
subfiles.about: Records U.S. officials' views on crab tariffs and the threat to Alaskan salmon.
subfiles.summary: O'Malley and colleagues discuss a possible agreement to protect salmon runs, tariff concessions, and wider international conservation. They favor awaiting developments before opening negotiations.

subfiles.title: Navy warning on Japanese activities in Aleutian harbors
subfiles.from: C. F. Adams, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards reports alleging Japanese collection of military information in the Aleutians.
subfiles.summary: Calls the reported conduct improper and provides two report excerpts.

subfiles.title: Bering Sea Patrol report excerpts on Japanese visits
subfiles.about: Describes Japanese vessels and visitors at Attu, Atka, and Unalaska.
subfiles.summary: Witnesses recount visits by Hakuho Maru and Kokusai Maru, photography, scientific collecting, and inquiries about fisheries and island waters. The report identifies journalists, photographers, and men with naval or fisheries connections, while noting uncertainty about some suspected activities.

subfiles.title: Navy survey expedition report excerpts
subfiles.about: Adds witness accounts concerning Kokusai Maru's 1931 Aleutian voyage.
subfiles.summary: Accounts describe extensive photography around Unalaska and Dutch Harbor and questioning about local waters. One witness suspected the announced goodwill flight was a cover. The report also discusses botanist Eric Hultén and explicitly notes disagreement about suspicions concerning him.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Navy intelligence reports
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Navy reports about alleged Japanese intelligence gathering.
subfiles.summary: Says the material is receiving careful consideration.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Siam fisheries despatch
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on Shonan Maru's arrival in Siam.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Potter's November 12, 1932 despatch.

subfiles.title: Excerpt on Shonan Maru's Bangkok visit
subfiles.about: Describes local concern about a Japanese fisheries research vessel's Bangkok visit.
subfiles.summary: The Shonan Maru demonstrated equipment to fisheries officials. Local fishermen feared Japanese competition and discussed possible licensing and treaty constraints.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Pacific fisheries letter
subfiles.about: Points to a letter on Japanese fisheries and government assistance.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a December 21, 1932 association letter.

subfiles.title: War Department forwards follow-up on Japanese fishermen
subfiles.about: Forwards the governor general's follow-up on the Philippine boat seizures.
subfiles.summary: Page 223 repeats the letter on page 222.

subfiles.title: Governor general's follow-up on Arayat incident
subfiles.from: Governor General of the Philippine Islands
subfiles.about: Reports the hearing and release of Japanese crews seized near Fuga Island.
subfiles.summary: A customs hearing found both boats fishing without licenses; the fishermen reported fair treatment. The Japanese vice-consul accepted the findings, the 34 men were released to the consul general, and the governor general considered the case closed.

subfiles.title: Philippine seizure papers sent to Grew
subfiles.about: Forwards War Department correspondence on the December 1932 boat seizures.
subfiles.summary: Sends both letters and their enclosures.

subfiles.title: Two Japanese canneries depart for Bering Sea
subfiles.about: Reports Taihoku Maru and Shohei Maru departing Hakodate for crab fishing.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says they will fish offshore and avoid American ports.

subfiles.title: Cannery departures reported to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew's telegram on two Japanese floating canneries.
subfiles.summary: Identifies their planned Bering Sea voyage.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledges cannery information
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the report on the two floating canneries.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will observe the fishery and report developments.

subfiles.title: Internal note on cannery launches
subfiles.about: Notes that two Japanese canneries will have five auxiliary launches.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Tokyo despatch No. 375.

subfiles.title: Auxiliary launches for 1933 canneries
subfiles.about: Identifies the launches accompanying Taihoku Maru and Shohei Maru.
subfiles.summary: Lists three launches for Taihoku Maru and two for Shohei Maru, with tonnages.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to veterans' letter
subfiles.about: Points to a letter opposing Japanese-owned fishing vessels and seafood imports.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a February 26, 1934 letter.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to proposed fishing-vessel legislation
subfiles.about: Points to Commerce correspondence on Pacific fishing vessels and proposed legislation.
subfiles.summary: The note mentions an amendment to Revised Statutes section 4311.

subfiles.title: Internal assessment of Kobe fisheries report
subfiles.about: Assesses the relevance of McClintock's report on Japanese fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the Soviet-Japanese dispute and possible Nichiro-Kyodo merger.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese fisheries
subfiles.about: Begins an analysis of Japanese fisheries, especially Soviet fishery rentals and exchange rates.
subfiles.summary: The report's title page and contents precede a discussion of Japanese fishing rights under the Portsmouth treaty and the 1928 convention. It explains earlier rental-payment problems, the 1931 Shidehara-Troyanovsky exchange arrangement, and the Soviet proposal in 1934 to raise the rate from 32½ to 75 sen per ruble. The account of the resulting diplomatic dispute continues beyond page 240.
